engineFindings.summary: subtract() robustness on the Zoo engine is tool-shape- and scale-dependent. Failing (deterministic, 'The Zoo engine cannot handle this 3D subtraction yet'): wedge-prism subtract after an opening subtract; 3-profile loft cutter (straight walls + flare) at 40x40 panel scale and at chamfer 0.8 even at 60x60 scale; multi-tool single subtract of opening+wedges; wedge chains crossing prior wedge grooves. Passing: straight prism subtract; convex 2-profile frustum loft subtract; prism-then-frustum and frustum-then-prism sequences; the f4 Text-to-CAD 3-profile loft at exactly 60x60/30/chamfer 0.5; the insert's 4-wedge chain on a plain extrusion. Fix shipped: rect panel now cuts with opening prism + 2-profile chamfer frustum (two simple booleans).
